Opinion: How Souls to the Polls showed up for the community on Election Day

by Rick Deines, Milwaukee Neighborhood News Service
November 16, 2026

Milwaukee Neighborhood News Service invites community members to submit opinion pieces of 500-800 words on topics of interest to central city Milwaukee. To send a submission for consideration, please email info@milwaukeenns.org. The views expressed are solely those of the authors.

On Nov. 3, well over 300 Milwaukee residents were the recipients of rides to their polling locations. 

Most had no other option — Souls to the Polls met the need. 

They’ve been at it for years. The inspiration came from the churches in the 1960s South that shuttled Black people to vote for the first time.

In Milwaukee I experienced, as a volunteer driver, a remarkable determination, resilience and commitment of persons to participate in those systems that too often have ignored and underserved them.

Rain, lack of mobility and other obstacles deterred no one that I rode with — quite a privilege for me to be invited to connect with my neighbors in the central city.

Ms. Norma J. Ballentine provides the inspired leadership. 

She is a clear example of how we can be together as a shared community desiring participatorial unity. Her colleague David was ever ready with technical assistance and connected conversation. 

Everything was carefully organized and calibrated in a way that gave us all a sense of ”‘team’” across the spectrum of drivers and riders. Her energy and giant life spirit gives everyone a sense of purpose.

Souls to the Polls gets my vote for MVP this week. Thanks to all who make it work!

What a week that was!

Rick Deines is a trained facilitator for Civil Community Conversation and advocate for men in recovery through Serenity Inns.
